scenes.heading: Why the sea breathes twice a day
scenes.narration: Twice a day, the ocean rises and falls. Here is why.

scenes.heading: Three forces at play
items: The Moon's gravity pulls the water
The Sun adds a smaller pull
scenes.narration: Three things are at play. The Moon's gravity pulls on the oceans, the Sun adds a smaller pull, and the Earth spins underneath it all.

scenes.label: of the Moon's pull is what the Sun adds
scenes.source: Ratio of solar to lunar tidal force
scenes.narration: The Sun is huge, but far away. Its tidal pull is only about forty six percent of the Moon's.

scenes.heading: Spring vs neap tides

left.title: Spring tides
left.text: Sun and Moon line up. Bigger highs, lower lows.

right.title: Neap tides
right.text: They pull at right angles. Gentler tides.

scenes.narration: When the Sun and Moon line up, their pulls add together and we get spring tides. When they pull at right angles, we get gentle neap tides.

scenes.heading: Two bulges, one spinning planet
scenes.narration: So, two bulges of water and one spinning planet. That's the whole trick.
